about: Business frameworks for consult-on-board. Summaries are written for this skill. guideJa is the gray guide under the title of a Japanese frame. An entry with skill is drawn by that skill of the plugin and has no shape or cells. shape and cells feed scripts/frame.js: the frame spec is { shape, ...cells }.

frameworks.name: 3 Gen Principles
frameworks.summary: Go to the real place, see the real thing, and check the real facts before you judge.
frameworks.whenToUse: The talk runs on reports and guesses; nobody has looked at the actual site.
frameworks.guideJa:
思い込みでなく、事実で判断するための型。
現場で見たこと・現物・数字を書く。
checks: Each row holds what was seen on site, the real thing, or a real number, not hearsay or a guess.

rows: What we saw 見たこと

frameworks.name: 3C Analysis
frameworks.summary: Look at the market from three sides: the customers, the competitors, and your own company.
frameworks.whenToUse: A plan or product idea needs a quick check of where it stands in its market.
frameworks.guideJa:
市場での立ち位置を確かめる型。
顧客・競合・自社のそれぞれで気づいたことを書く。
checks: Customer, Competitor and Company items sit in their own box.
Facts, not plans.

frameworks.name: 3M (Muri, Muda, Mura)
frameworks.summary: Find overload, waste, and unevenness in a piece of work.
frameworks.whenToUse: Work feels heavy or slow and the person cannot say where the loss is.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事のロスを見つける型。
無理・無駄・ムラが出ている所を書く。
checks: Muri is load beyond capacity, Muda adds no value, Mura varies by day or person.
Each names a place in the work.

rows: Where we see it 見られる所

frameworks.name: 4P (Marketing Mix)
frameworks.summary: Decide what to sell, at what price, through which channel, and how to make it known.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product exists and the way to bring it to market is unclear or inconsistent.
frameworks.guideJa:
売り方を一貫させる型。
製品・価格・売る場所・知らせ方を決めて書く。
checks: All four are decided for the same target customer and fit each other (e.g. a high price matches the product and channel).

frameworks.name: Five Forces
frameworks.summary: Judge how attractive an industry is from five pressures on its profit.
frameworks.whenToUse: The question is whether to enter or stay in a market, or why profit is thin.
frameworks.guideJa:
業界がもうかるかを見る型。
中心の競争に効く 4 つの力の強さを書く。
checks: All five forces look at one industry and one position in it.
Each force has a strength (strong or weak) and a reason.

frameworks.name: 5 Whys
frameworks.summary: Ask why again and again until the answer is a cause you can act on.
frameworks.whenToUse: A problem keeps coming back after quick fixes.

frameworks.name: 5S
frameworks.summary: Keep a workplace usable: sort, set in order, shine, standardize, sustain.
frameworks.whenToUse: Things are hard to find, the place is messy, or good habits fade.
frameworks.guideJa:
職場を使いやすく保つ型。
5 つの項目ごとに、今の様子とやることを書く。
checks: Sort removes what is not needed before Set in order gives places; the steps build in order.
Each item is a concrete state of this workplace.

items: Seiton 整頓 set in order

frameworks.name: 5W1H
frameworks.summary: Pin down who, what, when, where, why, and how.
frameworks.whenToUse: A plan or report is vague and parts are missing.
frameworks.guideJa:
抜けのない計画にする型。
6 つの問いに 1 つずつ答える。
checks: All six answers are about the same one matter and do not contradict each other.
Why states the purpose.

frameworks.name: 6W2H
frameworks.summary: 5W1H plus for whom and how much, for plans that need a target and a budget.
frameworks.whenToUse: A plan must be complete enough to approve or to hand over.
frameworks.guideJa:
承認や引き継ぎに足る計画にする型。
8 つの問いに 1 つずつ答える。
checks: As 5W1H; Whom names the receiver, and How much has a number (budget or price).

frameworks.name: 7S Framework
frameworks.summary: Check whether strategy, structure, systems and the softer parts of an organization fit together.
frameworks.whenToUse: A change program stalls, or a strategy does not show up in daily work.
frameworks.guideJa:
組織がかみ合っているかを見る型。
中心の価値観と 6 つの要素の今の姿を書く。
checks: All seven describe the same organization now.
Shared values sit in the center, and each of the others is checked for fit with it and each other.

frameworks.name: AARRR (Pirate Metrics)
frameworks.summary: Follow users through five stages of growth and find the stage that leaks most.
frameworks.whenToUse: A service grows slowly and the team does not know which stage to fix.
frameworks.guideJa:
伸び悩む段階を見つける型。
5 つの段階ごとに、人数や率を書く。
checks: Stages follow in order, each with a count or a rate.
A later stage is not larger than the one before it.

frameworks.name: ABC Model
frameworks.summary: Separate the event, the belief about it, and the feeling or action that follows.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person is upset and mixes what happened with how they read it.
frameworks.guideJa:
出来事と受け止め方を分ける型。
出来事・どう受け止めたか・その結果を書く。
checks: A is the fact that happened, B is how the person took it (a belief), C is a feeling or an action.
C follows from B, not from A alone.

frameworks.name: Affinity Diagram (KJ Method)
frameworks.summary: Write each fact or idea on its own note, then group the notes by feel and name each group.
frameworks.whenToUse: Many loose ideas or voices are on the table and no order is visible.
frameworks.guideJa:
ばらばらの意見をまとめる型。
似たものを集めて、グループに名前を付ける。
checks: One note holds one fact or idea.
Each group name is a sentence that says what its notes share.
Each note is in one group only.

branches: Group A グループ A
Group B グループ B
Group C グループ C
Group D グループ D

frameworks.name: AIDMA
frameworks.summary: Trace a buyer from first notice to purchase in five mental steps.
frameworks.whenToUse: Promotion works for some steps but sales do not follow.
frameworks.guideJa:
買うまでの気持ちの流れを見る型。
5 つの段階で、相手がどう動くかを書く。
checks: The steps follow one buyer in order.
Items in each step are that mental state or an action that moves the buyer to it.

frameworks.name: Ansoff Matrix
frameworks.nameJa: アンゾフの成長マトリクス
frameworks.summary: Sort growth options by new or existing products and new or existing markets.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person wants growth and has several directions in mind.
frameworks.guideJa:
成長の方向を選ぶ型。
製品と市場の新旧で、案を 4 つの所に置く。
checks: Each item is placed by own product (existing or new) and market (existing or new).

frameworks.name: AQAL (Integral Model)
frameworks.summary: See a matter from inside and outside, and from one person and the group.
frameworks.whenToUse: A problem is seen only from one side, for example only as a system or only as a feeling.
frameworks.guideJa:
物事を 4 つの見方でとらえる型。
個人と集団、内面と外面の 4 つの所に書く。
checks: Each quadrant views the same matter from its side (interior or exterior, individual or collective).

frameworks.name: As-Is / To-Be
frameworks.summary: Put the current state next to the wanted state; the gap is the work.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person knows something is wrong but cannot say what good looks like.
frameworks.guideJa:
今とありたい姿の差をつかむ型。
今・ありたい姿・その差を並べて書く。
checks: Both sides compare the same item.
The Gap is the difference for that item.

frameworks.name: Balanced Scorecard
frameworks.nameJa: バランススコアカード
frameworks.origin: Robert S. Kaplan, David P. Norton
frameworks.summary: Set goals and measures from four views, not money only.
frameworks.whenToUse: Targets are all financial and the drivers behind them are missing.
frameworks.guideJa:
お金以外の目標も持つ型。
4 つの視点ごとに、目標と測り方を書く。
checks: Each view has a goal, a measure and a target value.
Lower views support upper ones (learning, process, customer, finance).

rows:
Internal process
業務プロセス

frameworks.name: Brainstorming
frameworks.nameJa: ブレインストーミング
frameworks.summary: Gather many ideas fast; judge them later.
frameworks.whenToUse: The group needs options and early judging blocks new ideas.
frameworks.guideJa:
案をたくさん出す型。
良し悪しは後で決める。思いついた順に線の先へ書く。
checks: There is one question.
Each branch is an idea for it, with no judgment or criticism.
Quantity comes first.

frameworks.name: Brainwriting (6-3-5)
frameworks.nameJa: ブレインライティング
frameworks.summary: Each person writes ideas silently and builds on the ideas of the others in rounds.
frameworks.whenToUse: A few loud voices lead the talk, or people are shy to speak.
frameworks.guideJa:
全員が黙って案を出す型。
1 人 3 つずつ書き、次の人がそれを広げる。
checks: Ideas in each round build on the ideas of the round before.
Ideas answer the question; judging comes later.

frameworks.name: Brand Equity
frameworks.nameJa: ブランド・エクイティ
frameworks.summary: Check the value a brand name adds: loyalty, awareness, perceived quality, associations, other assets.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person asks why customers pay more, or less, for the brand.
frameworks.guideJa:
ブランドの価値を見る型。
5 つの要素ごとに、今の様子を書く。
checks: All five are about the same one brand and state its current state with facts or numbers.

frameworks.name: Business Flowchart
frameworks.summary: Draw who does which step in which order.
frameworks.whenToUse: Hand-offs are unclear or a process needs to be explained.
frameworks.guideJa:
誰がどの順で何をするかを見る型。
担当の行と手順の列で、作業を書く。
checks: Each step sits in the lane of the person who does it.
Steps connect in order with a start and an end.

frameworks.name: Improvement Proposal Sheet
frameworks.summary: One page that states the problem, its cause, the change, and the effect.
frameworks.whenToUse: A worker has an improvement idea and needs to put it to a manager.
frameworks.guideJa:
改善案を 1 枚で伝える型。
問題・原因・提案・効果・費用を書く。
checks: The cause produces the problem.
The proposal removes the cause.
The effect is how much the problem shrinks; the cost is a number.

frameworks.name: Business Model Canvas
frameworks.nameJa: ビジネスモデルキャンバス
frameworks.summary: Lay out a business model in nine connected areas on one sheet.
frameworks.whenToUse: A new business or an existing one must be seen as a whole.
frameworks.guideJa:
事業の全体を 1 枚で見る型。
9 つの区画に、自分の事業のことを書く。
checks: The nine areas connect through the same customer segments.
The value proposition reaches them through channels; revenue and cost match the activities and resources.

areas.label:
Customer Relationships
顧客との関係

Customer Segments
顧客セグメント

frameworks.name: Career Anchors
frameworks.summary: Find the one value a person will not give up in a career, out of eight types.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person is unsure about a job change or feels lost in a career.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事で譲れない価値を見つける型。
8 つの価値のうち、心に響くものに印を付ける。
checks: One anchor is chosen for one person.
The reason is the person's own experience of what they would not give up.

frameworks.name: CMMI
frameworks.nameJa: CMMI（能力成熟度モデル統合）
frameworks.summary: Rate how mature the processes of an organization are, in five levels.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team wants to know where its process stands and what the next level asks.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事の進め方の成熟度を見る型。
今どの段にいて、次に何が要るかを書く。
checks: Each item matches the traits of its level.
The current level meets every level below it.

frameworks.name: Cognition-Behavior Loop
frameworks.summary: See how a way of thinking leads to an action, its result, and back to the thinking.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person or team repeats the same pattern and wants to break it.
frameworks.guideJa:
くり返すパターンをほどく型。
考え・気持ち・行動・結果の輪を書く。
checks: Thought leads to feeling, action and result, and the result feeds the next thought in one loop.

frameworks.name: Generic Competitive Strategies
frameworks.summary: Choose to win by low cost or by difference, in a wide or a narrow market.
frameworks.whenToUse: The company tries to be everything and has no clear edge.
frameworks.guideJa:
どう勝つかを選ぶ型。
安さか違いか、広くか狭くかで、自分の位置を決める。
checks: One business picks one quadrant.
It does not chase low cost and differentiation at once.

quadrants: Cost leadership コスト・リーダーシップ

frameworks.name: Contradiction Integration Map
frameworks.summary: Write two goals that pull against each other, then look for a way that serves both.
frameworks.whenToUse: The talk is stuck in an either-or choice.
frameworks.guideJa:
あちらを立てればこちらが立たない時の型。
2 つの望みと、両方を満たす案を書く。
checks: A and B are two wants that truly pull against each other.
The both-way idea meets both A and B.

columns: Want A 求めること A
Want B 求めること B

frameworks.name: Controllable / Uncontrollable
frameworks.nameJa: コントロール可能・不可能
frameworks.summary: Split concerns into what you can change and what you cannot.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person worries about many things and spends energy where it changes nothing.
frameworks.guideJa:
力を注ぐ所を決める型。
心配ごとを、変えられる・働きかけられる・変えられないに分ける。
checks: Each item sits in exactly one column by what the person can do about it.
Actions go to the first two columns.

columns: Can influence 働きかけられる
Cannot control 変えられない

frameworks.name: Core Competence
frameworks.nameJa: コア・コンピタンス分析
frameworks.summary: Find the skills that give customers value, are hard to copy, and open many markets.
frameworks.whenToUse: The company asks what it is truly good at before it expands.
frameworks.guideJa:
本当の強みを見つける型。
能力ごとに、顧客の価値・まねしにくさ・広がりを書く。
checks: Each ability answers all three tests: customer value, hard to copy, reach.
Missing one means it is not core.

rows: Hard to copy 模倣困難

frameworks.name: Customer Journey Map
frameworks.nameJa: カスタマージャーニーマップ
frameworks.summary: Follow one customer through each stage, with actions, touch points, and feelings.
frameworks.whenToUse: Customers drop out or complain, and nobody sees the whole experience.
frameworks.guideJa:
お客の体験を通しで見る型。
段階ごとに、行動・接点・気持ち・課題を書く。
checks: One persona on one journey.
Action, touch point, feeling and issue of each stage belong to that stage.
Stages run in time order.

frameworks.name: Decision Matrix
frameworks.summary: Score each option against weighted criteria and compare the totals.
frameworks.whenToUse: Several options look fine and the choice keeps going round.
frameworks.guideJa:
案を比べて選ぶ型。
基準に重みを付け、案ごとに点を入れて合計する。
checks: Each criterion has a weight.
Total is the sum of weight x score.

frameworks.name: Diffusion of Innovations
frameworks.summary: New things spread through five adopter groups, from innovators to laggards.
frameworks.whenToUse: A new product sells to early fans but does not reach the mass market.
frameworks.guideJa:
新しい物が広まる順を見る型。
今どの層まで届いているかを書く。
checks: Items in each group match the traits of that group.
A gap (chasm) lies between early adopters and the majority.

frameworks.name: ECRS
frameworks.summary: Improve work in this order: eliminate, combine, rearrange, simplify.
frameworks.whenToUse: A process is slow and the person wants ideas to make it lighter.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事を軽くする案を出す型。
なくす・まとめる・入れ替える・単純にするの順に考える。
checks: Ideas are tried in order: eliminate, combine, rearrange, simplify.
All ideas are about the same one piece of work.

frameworks.name: Empathy Map
frameworks.summary: Write what a user says, thinks, does, and feels, to understand them.
frameworks.whenToUse: The team talks about users in general terms and lacks a real picture.
frameworks.guideJa:
相手を深く知る型。
相手が言う・考える・する・感じることを書く。
checks: All four are about one user.
Says and Does are observed; Thinks and Feels are inferred, and they are kept apart.

frameworks.name: Event Proposal
frameworks.summary: One sheet with the aim, audience, date, place, program, budget, and expected result of an event.
frameworks.whenToUse: An event idea must be approved or shared.
frameworks.guideJa:
イベントの企画を 1 枚にする型。
目的・対象・日時・内容・予算・効果を書く。
checks: The expected result answers the aim.
Audience, date, program and budget fit the aim.

frameworks.name: Expectation / Issue Matrix
frameworks.nameJa: 期待・課題マトリクス
frameworks.summary: List what each stakeholder expects next to the issues that block it.
frameworks.whenToUse: Several parties want different things and the priorities are unclear.
frameworks.guideJa:
関係者の期待と課題を並べる型。
人ごとに、期待・課題・優先度を書く。
checks: In each row, the issue is what blocks that person's expectation.
Priority follows from the size of the expectation and the weight of the issue.

frameworks.name: Experiential Learning Cycle
frameworks.summary: Learn from experience: do, reflect, draw a lesson, try it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person wants to grow from what happened, good or bad.
frameworks.guideJa:
経験から学ぶ型。
やったこと・振り返り・教訓・次の試みを輪で書く。
checks: Experience, reflection, concept and experiment follow from the same one experience.
The experiment tests the lesson drawn.

frameworks.name: FABE
frameworks.summary: Build a sales talk from feature, advantage, benefit, and evidence.
frameworks.whenToUse: A pitch lists features but does not say why the buyer should care.
frameworks.guideJa:
売り込みの話を組み立てる型。
特徴・利点・相手の得・証拠の順に書く。
checks: Feature is a fact, advantage follows from it, benefit is what the buyer gains, evidence is a fact that shows the benefit.

frameworks.name: Fishbone Diagram
frameworks.nameJa: 特性要因図（フィッシュボーン）
frameworks.summary: Sort the possible causes of one problem into bones such as people, method, machine, material.
frameworks.whenToUse: A problem has many possible causes and the talk jumps between them.
frameworks.guideJa:
原因を漏れなく洗い出す型。
右に問題を書き、骨ごとに思い当たる原因を書く。
checks: The head is one problem.
Each bone is a kind of cause; items under it are causes, not measures.

frameworks.name: Force Field Analysis
frameworks.nameJa: フォースフィールド分析
frameworks.summary: List the forces that push a change forward against the forces that hold it back.
frameworks.whenToUse: A change is planned and the person wants to know what will help or block it.
frameworks.guideJa:
変化を助ける力と妨げる力を比べる型。
両側に、それぞれの力を書く。
checks: Both sides are about the same one change.
Each force can carry a strength score so the sides can be compared.

frameworks.name: Funnel Analysis
frameworks.summary: Count how many people pass each step toward a goal and where they drop out.
frameworks.whenToUse: Visitors or leads are many but results are few.
frameworks.guideJa:
どこで人が減るかを見る型。
段階ごとに、人数と次へ進む率を書く。
checks: Stages run in order, each with a count.
A later stage is not larger.
The biggest drop is visible.

frameworks.name: Gantt Chart
frameworks.summary: Show tasks as bars on a time axis.
frameworks.whenToUse: Work has several tasks and the schedule is in people's heads.
frameworks.guideJa:
予定を見える形にする型。
作業の行ごとに、いつからいつまでを書く。
checks: Each task has a start and an end.
A task that depends on another starts after it.

frameworks.name: GROW Model
frameworks.summary: Coach with four questions: goal, reality, options, will.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person wants to move but does not know where to start.
frameworks.guideJa:
目標に向けて動き出す型。
目標・今の状態・選べる道・やると決めたことを書く。
checks: Goal, reality, options and will follow in order.
Options close the gap between goal and reality.
Will is the next action the person chooses.

frameworks.name: Heinrich's Law
frameworks.summary: Behind one serious accident lie many minor ones and many more near misses.
frameworks.whenToUse: Small incidents are ignored and the person fears a big one.
frameworks.guideJa:
小さな異常から大事故を防ぐ型。
各段に、最近あった出来事を書く。
checks: All three levels are about the same kind of accident.
Lower levels (near misses) hold more cases.

levels: 300 Near misses ヒヤリ・ハット

frameworks.name: How Might We
frameworks.summary: Turn a problem into an open question that invites ideas.
frameworks.whenToUse: The problem is clear but the team only complains about it.
frameworks.guideJa:
問題を、案を出せる問いに変える型。
「どうすれば〜できるか」の形で問いを書く。
checks: Each line is a "How might we" question, open to many ideas, not one answer in disguise.

items: How might we ...? どうすれば:
How might we ...? どうすれば…?
How might we ...? どうすれば…?

frameworks.name: Idea Sheet
frameworks.summary: Capture one idea with its target, value, way, and next step.
frameworks.whenToUse: Ideas are thrown out but not kept in a form others can judge.
frameworks.guideJa:
思いつきを判断できる形にする型。
案・誰に・価値・方法・次の一歩を書く。
checks: The value is what the For whom person gains.
How delivers that value.
The next step is a concrete action that can start now.

frameworks.name: Interrelationship Digraph
frameworks.summary: Link causes with arrows to find the ones that drive most others.
frameworks.whenToUse: Causes affect each other in loops and a simple list does not fit.
frameworks.guideJa:
からみ合う原因の中心を見つける型。
原因を矢印でつなぎ、矢印が多く出る所を探す。
checks: Arrows point from cause to effect.
A factor with many outgoing arrows is a candidate root cause.

frameworks.name: Issue Setting Sheet
frameworks.summary: State the issue, its background, the goal, and the scope before solving.
frameworks.whenToUse: People start solving before they agree on what the issue is.
frameworks.guideJa:
解く前に課題をそろえる型。
課題・背景・目指す姿・範囲・担当を書く。
checks: The issue states one thing to solve.
The goal is the state when it is solved.
Scope and owner are set.

frameworks.name: Johari Window
frameworks.summary: Sort what is known about a person by whether they and others know it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person wants feedback or to understand a gap in how others see them.
frameworks.guideJa:
自分の見え方の差を知る型。
自分と他人が知っているかで、4 つの所に書く。
checks: Each item fits one window by whether the self knows it and whether others know it.
Blind spot items come from others.

axes.left: 自分が知る Known to self
axes.right: 自分は知らない Unknown to self
axes.top: 他人が知る Known to others
axes.bottom: 他人は知らない Unknown to others

frameworks.name: Kanban Board
frameworks.summary: Show work items in columns by state and limit work in progress.
frameworks.whenToUse: Too many tasks are open and nobody sees the flow.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事の流れを見る型。
作業を、やること・作業中・完了の列に置く。
checks: Each item is in one column only.
Doing has a limit.
Items move left to right only.

frameworks.name: Katz Skill Model
frameworks.summary: The mix of technical, human, and conceptual skills a manager needs changes with the level.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person is promoted and asks which skills to build next.
frameworks.guideJa:
立場ごとに要る力を見る型。
層ごとに、3 つの力がどれほど要るかを書く。
checks: Conceptual skill grows toward the top, technical skill toward the bottom.
Human skill is needed at every level.

frameworks.name: KPI Tree
frameworks.summary: Break a top goal into the measures that make it up, down to ones a team can move.
frameworks.whenToUse: The goal is a big number and nobody knows which lever to pull.
frameworks.guideJa:
大きな目標を動かせる数字に分ける型。
右へ行くほど、自分たちで動かせる数字にする。
checks: The root is a KGI with a number.
Children add or multiply to the parent.
Deeper numbers are ones the team can move.

frameworks.name: KPT
frameworks.summary: Look back with three columns: keep, problem, try.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team ends a sprint or a project and wants to improve the next one.
frameworks.guideJa:
振り返りの型。
続けること・困ったこと・次に試すことを書く。
checks: Each Try solves a Problem or extends a Keep.

frameworks.name: Lanchester Strategy
frameworks.origin: Frederick W. Lanchester; applied by Nobuo Taoka
frameworks.summary: A strong player fights wide and by mass; a weak player picks a narrow field and focuses.
frameworks.whenToUse: A small company competes with big ones and spreads too thin.
frameworks.guideJa:
強者と弱者で戦い方を変える型。
自分はどちらか、どう戦うかを書く。
checks: The person first decides from market share whether they are the leader or the challenger.
A challenger focuses on a narrow field.

frameworks.name: Lewin's Change Model
frameworks.nameJa: レヴィンの組織変革モデル
frameworks.summary: Change in three steps: unfreeze the old way, change, refreeze the new way.
frameworks.whenToUse: A change was announced but people keep the old habits.
frameworks.guideJa:
変化を根付かせる型。
古いやり方を溶かす・変える・固めるの順に書く。
checks: Unfreeze, change and refreeze follow in order.
Unfreeze gives the reason to change; refreeze makes the new way the rule.

frameworks.name: Logic Tree
frameworks.summary: Split a question into parts without gaps or overlaps, level by level.
frameworks.whenToUse: A big question feels too large to start on.
frameworks.guideJa:
大きな問いを小さく分ける型。
漏れと重なりが無いように、右へ分けていく。
checks: The root is a question or a goal.
Each parent equals its children together (causes or means).
Siblings are one kind and one level, with no overlap.

frameworks.name: Management Hierarchy
frameworks.summary: Layers of management, from top to front line, and what each decides.
frameworks.whenToUse: Roles of the layers are unclear and decisions go to the wrong level.
frameworks.guideJa:
層ごとの役割を見る型。
各層が決めること・やることを書く。
checks: Each layer states what it decides.
Higher layers decide longer-term and wider matters.

levels: Front line 現場リーダー

frameworks.name: Mandalart
frameworks.summary: Put a theme in the center of a 3x3 grid and fill the eight cells around it; each can become a new center.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person needs many concrete actions for one goal.
frameworks.guideJa:
1 つの目標から行動を出す型。
真ん中にテーマ、まわり 8 つに関わることを書く。
checks: All eight cells around the center are parts that achieve the center theme, with no overlap.

frameworks.name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
frameworks.nameJa: マズローの欲求段階説
frameworks.summary: Needs build up in five levels, from body needs to self-actualization.
frameworks.whenToUse: The question is what motivates a person or a customer.
frameworks.guideJa:
何が人を動かすかを見る型。
下の段から、満たされているかを書く。
checks: Items in each level match its need.
A higher need grows strong once the lower ones are met.

frameworks.name: Mind Map
frameworks.summary: Put a theme in the center and grow branches of related ideas.
frameworks.whenToUse: Thoughts come in no order and the person wants to see them all.
frameworks.guideJa:
考えを広げて全体を見る型。
真ん中のテーマから、思いつくことを枝の先に書く。
checks: Each branch comes from its parent branch.
Ideas get more concrete farther from the center.

frameworks.name: Morphological Analysis
frameworks.summary: List the dimensions of a problem and the options for each, then combine them.
frameworks.whenToUse: A new product or plan is wanted and obvious ideas are used up.
frameworks.guideJa:
組み合わせで新しい案を作る型。
要素ごとに選択肢を書き、組み合わせを選ぶ。
checks: The dimensions are independent.
Options of one dimension do not overlap.
A combination takes one option per dimension.

frameworks.name: Mission, Vision, Values
frameworks.summary: State why the organization exists, where it goes, and what it values.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team lacks a shared direction or its decisions conflict.
frameworks.guideJa:
組織の向きをそろえる型。
使命・目指す姿・大事にする価値を書く。
checks: Mission is why the organization exists, vision is the future it aims at, values guide behavior.
Lower levels support upper ones.

frameworks.name: Need / Want Matrix
frameworks.summary: Separate what a person truly needs from the concrete thing they ask for.
frameworks.whenToUse: Customers ask for features and the team builds them without knowing why.
frameworks.guideJa:
言われた要望の奥を見る型。
欲しいと言うものと、本当に必要なことを分けて書く。
checks: In each row, the need is the real purpose behind the want (why the person wants it).

columns: Want 欲しいと言うもの
Need 本当に必要なこと

frameworks.name: OARR
frameworks.summary: Open a meeting with its outcome, agenda, roles, and rules.
frameworks.whenToUse: Meetings drift and end without a result.
frameworks.guideJa:
会議を締める型。
始めに、ゴール・議題・役割・ルールを決めて書く。
checks: The outcome is what the meeting produces by its end.
The agenda leads to it.
Roles and rules fit the meeting.

frameworks.name: Occupational Stress Model (NIOSH)
frameworks.nameJa: 職業性ストレスモデル
frameworks.summary: Job stressors lead to strain, shaped by personal factors, outside factors, and support.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person or team is worn out and the sources are mixed up.
frameworks.guideJa:
疲れの元を分けて見る型。
ストレスの元・やわらげるもの・反応・不調を書く。
checks: Stressors lead to reactions and then illness.
Moderators act between stressors and reactions.

steps: Stressors 仕事のストレス要因
Moderators 個人・仕事外・支援

frameworks.name: Organizational Chart
frameworks.summary: Show units and reporting lines.
frameworks.whenToUse: Who reports to whom is unclear, or a new structure is planned.
frameworks.guideJa:
誰が誰に報告するかを見る型。
組織の名前と長を、線でつないで書く。
checks: Each unit has one head above it.
Reporting lines reach the top without a break.

frameworks.name: Pareto Analysis
frameworks.summary: Sort causes by size; a few of them make most of the effect.
frameworks.whenToUse: Many small problems compete for attention.
frameworks.guideJa:
効く所から手を付ける型。
原因を大きい順に並べ、上位の数件を見る。
checks: Causes are sorted from largest.
The cumulative line ends at 100%.
It shows whether a few causes make most of the effect.

frameworks.name: Payoff Matrix
frameworks.summary: Place ideas by effect and ease to pick the ones worth doing first.
frameworks.whenToUse: There are many ideas and few resources.
frameworks.guideJa:
やる案を選ぶ型。
効果と手軽さで、案を 4 つの所に置く。
checks: Each idea sits in one quadrant by effect and ease.
All ideas are placed with the same standards.

quadrants: If time allows 余裕があれば

frameworks.name: PDCA Cycle
frameworks.origin: Walter A. Shewhart; W. Edwards Deming
frameworks.summary: Plan, do, check, act, and repeat.
frameworks.whenToUse: Work is done once and not improved, or results are never checked.
frameworks.guideJa:
回しながら良くする型。
計画・実行・評価・改善を書き、また計画へ戻る。
checks: The plan has a measurable target.
Check compares the result with that target.
Act feeds the next plan.

frameworks.name: PERT Chart
frameworks.summary: Draw tasks as a network with their order and times to find the critical path.
frameworks.whenToUse: A project has many dependent tasks and the end date is at risk.
frameworks.guideJa:
作業の順と山場を見る型。
作業を順につなぎ、一番長い道を見つける。
checks: Tasks connect by dependency with arrows, and each has a time.
The longest path is the critical path.

frameworks.name: PEST Analysis
frameworks.summary: Scan the outside world: politics, economy, society, technology.
frameworks.whenToUse: A long-term plan needs the big trends around it.
frameworks.guideJa:
まわりの大きな流れを見る型。
政治・経済・社会・技術の変化を書く。
checks: Items are the macro environment (Political, Economic, Social, Technological), outside control.

frameworks.name: PM Theory
frameworks.summary: Rate leadership by its push for results (P) and its care for the group (M).
frameworks.whenToUse: A leader asks why the team performs or feels the way it does.
frameworks.guideJa:
リーダーの型を見る型。
成果への働き（P）とまとまりへの気配り（M）の強さで置く。
checks: One leader is placed in one quadrant by the strength of P (results) and M (care for the group).
The basis is observed behavior.

frameworks.name: Positioning Map
frameworks.nameJa: ポジショニングマップ
frameworks.summary: Place your offer and the rivals on two axes that buyers care about.
frameworks.whenToUse: The product looks like the others and needs a clear place.
frameworks.guideJa:
他と違う位置を見つける型。
お客が気にする 2 つの軸で、自分と他社を置く。
checks: Both axes are things buyers care about when they choose, and are independent.
Own offer and rivals sit on the same axes.

frameworks.name: PRAM Model
frameworks.summary: Negotiate for both sides: plan, build the relation, agree, maintain.
frameworks.whenToUse: A deal must work for both sides and last.
frameworks.guideJa:
双方が得する交渉の型。
計画・関係づくり・合意・維持を書く。
checks: Plan, relationship, agreement and maintenance follow in order.
The agreement gives both sides a gain.

frameworks.name: PREP Method
frameworks.summary: Say the point, the reason, an example, and the point again.
frameworks.whenToUse: A message or talk is long and hard to follow.
frameworks.guideJa:
話を分かりやすくする型。
結論・理由・例・結論の順に書く。
checks: The first and last points are the same claim.
The reason supports it, and the example shows the reason concretely.

frameworks.name: Process Map
frameworks.summary: Draw the steps of a process with inputs, outputs, and the people involved.
frameworks.whenToUse: A process has delays or errors and its steps are not written down.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事の手順を見える形にする型。
入力から出力まで、手順を順に書く。
checks: Steps connect without a break from input to output.
Each step has an owner and what goes in and out.

frameworks.name: Product Life Cycle
frameworks.summary: Sales of a product go through introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person asks why sales change and what to do in the current stage.
frameworks.guideJa:
売上の変わり方を見る型。
今どの時期かと、その時期にやることを書く。
checks: The current stage follows from the sales trend.
Actions fit that stage.

frameworks.name: Product Out / Market In
frameworks.nameJa: プロダクトアウト / マーケットイン
frameworks.summary: Start from what you can make, or start from what the market wants.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team argues whether to push its technology or follow the customer.
frameworks.guideJa:
作れる物と求められる物を比べる型。
両側に、それぞれを書く。
checks: Both sides are about the same product or business.
The market side holds customer voices or facts.

columns: Market in 求められるもの

frameworks.name: Product Portfolio Management (BCG Matrix)
frameworks.summary: Place businesses by market growth and relative share to decide where to invest.
frameworks.whenToUse: A company has several businesses and limited money.
frameworks.guideJa:
どの事業にお金を回すかを決める型。
成長率とシェアで、事業を 4 つの所に置く。
checks: Each business sits in one quadrant by market growth and relative share, judged with numbers.

frameworks.name: Product Proposal
frameworks.summary: One sheet with the concept, target, value, features, price, and numbers of a new product.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product idea must be approved.
frameworks.guideJa:
新商品の企画を 1 枚にする型。
コンセプト・対象・価値・特徴・価格・数字を書く。
checks: All items connect through the same one target customer.
The price fits the value.

frameworks.name: Pros and Cons List
frameworks.nameJa: メリット・デメリット
frameworks.summary: List the points for and against one choice side by side.
frameworks.whenToUse: A yes-or-no decision keeps going round in the head.
frameworks.guideJa:
1 つの選択の良し悪しを比べる型。
良い点と気になる点を、それぞれの側に書く。
checks: Both sides are about the same one choice.

frameworks.name: Psychological Safety Check
frameworks.nameJa: 心理的安全性チェック
frameworks.summary: Check whether team members feel safe to speak up, ask, and admit mistakes.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team stays quiet in meetings or hides problems.
frameworks.guideJa:
チームで本音が言えるかを見る型。
問いごとに、1〜5 の点を付ける。
checks: Each question has a score from 1 to 5.
Scores are members' answers about one team now.

rows:
Mistakes are not held against me
ミスを責められない

I can raise problems
問題を言い出せる

I can ask for help
助けを求められる

My skills are valued
自分の力が活かされる

frameworks.name: QCD
frameworks.summary: Judge work or a supplier by quality, cost, and delivery.
frameworks.whenToUse: Options or suppliers must be compared on the basics.
frameworks.guideJa:
品質・費用・納期で比べる型。
今と目標を書く。
checks: Quality, cost and delivery each have a number now and a target number.

frameworks.name: RACI Matrix
frameworks.summary: For each task, mark who does it, who answers for it, who is asked, and who is told.
frameworks.whenToUse: Tasks fall between people or everyone thinks someone else owns them.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事の担当をはっきりさせる型。
作業ごとに、R（する）A（責任）C（相談）I（報告）を入れる。
checks: Each task has exactly one A (accountable) and at least one R (responsible).

frameworks.name: RFM Analysis
frameworks.summary: Rank customers by how recently, how often, and how much they buy.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person wants to know which customers to care for first.
frameworks.guideJa:
大事なお客を見つける型。
最近・回数・金額で、お客を分ける。
checks: Each of the three measures has number bands for high, middle and low, the same for all customers.

frameworks.name: Risk Matrix
frameworks.summary: Place risks by how likely and how severe they are.
frameworks.whenToUse: Many risks are listed and the person must choose which to treat first.
frameworks.guideJa:
先に手を打つリスクを選ぶ型。
起こりやすさと影響の大きさで、リスクを置く。
checks: Each risk sits in one quadrant by likelihood and severity.
The response fits the quadrant.

frameworks.name: Roadmap
frameworks.summary: Show the goal and the main milestones over time, by area.
frameworks.whenToUse: A long plan needs to be shared and kept on track.
frameworks.guideJa:
長い計画を共有する型。
分野の行と時期の列に、節目を書く。
checks: Milestones run in time order.
The milestones of each lane lead to the final goal.

frameworks.name: SCAMPER
frameworks.summary: Get new ideas from an existing one with seven questions.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product or service needs a fresh twist.
frameworks.guideJa:
今ある物から新しい案を出す型。
7 つの問いごとに、案を書く。
checks: All seven ideas start from the same one existing thing.
Each idea takes the form of its question (substitute, combine, and so on).

rows: Put to other use 転用

frameworks.name: Scenario Planning
frameworks.nameJa: シナリオ・プランニング
frameworks.summary: Pick two key uncertainties as axes and describe the four futures they make.
frameworks.whenToUse: The future is uncertain and one forecast is not enough.
frameworks.guideJa:
先の見えない未来に備える型。
2 つの不確かなことを軸に、4 つの未来を書く。
checks: Both axes are uncertain factors with high impact, independent of each other.
Each scenario matches its pair of axis ends.

frameworks.name: Business Scheme Diagram
frameworks.summary: Draw the players of a business and the flows of goods, money, and information between them.
frameworks.whenToUse: A business involves several parties and the flows are hard to explain.
frameworks.guideJa:
事業の仕組みを見る型。
関わる人と、物・お金・情報の流れを矢印で書く。
checks: Each arrow carries goods, money or information.
The money flow comes back to the company.

frameworks.name: SECI Model
frameworks.summary: Knowledge turns from tacit to explicit and back in four modes.
frameworks.whenToUse: Know-how stays in a few heads and does not spread.
frameworks.guideJa:
知恵をみんなのものにする型。
4 つの段階で、知恵がどう伝わるかを書く。
checks: Socialization, externalization, combination and internalization follow in order, turning tacit and explicit knowledge into each other.

frameworks.name: SMART Goals
frameworks.summary: Check that a goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.
frameworks.whenToUse: A goal is vague and nobody can tell when it is met.
frameworks.guideJa:
目標をはっきりさせる型。
5 つの問いに、はい・いいえと直し方を書く。
checks: The goal has a number and a date.
Each of the five has yes or no.

frameworks.name: Social Styles
frameworks.origin: David W. Merrill, Roger H. Reid
frameworks.summary: Sort how people communicate by how much they assert and how much they show feelings.
frameworks.whenToUse: Two people talk past each other.
frameworks.guideJa:
相手との話し方を合わせる型。
主張の強さと感情の出し方で、相手と自分を置く。
checks: One person is placed in one style by how much they assert and show feelings.
The basis is observed behavior.

frameworks.name: Stakeholder Analysis
frameworks.nameJa: ステークホルダー分析
frameworks.summary: Place the people involved by their influence and their interest.
frameworks.whenToUse: A project needs support and the person does not know whom to win first.
frameworks.guideJa:
誰をまず味方にするかを決める型。
影響力と関心で、関わる人を置く。
checks: Each person sits in one quadrant by power and interest.
The way to engage fits the quadrant.

axes.top: 影響力 大 High power
axes.bottom: 影響力 小 Low power

quadrants: Manage closely 重点的に関わる
Keep informed 情報を届ける

frameworks.name: Storyboard
frameworks.summary: Tell how a user meets a product as a row of scenes.
frameworks.whenToUse: An idea is abstract and needs to be felt as an experience.
frameworks.guideJa:
使う場面を物語にする型。
場面ごとに、何が起きるかを書く。
checks: Scenes follow one user in time order.
Each scene shows what the user does or feels.

frameworks.name: STP
frameworks.summary: Divide the market, choose the target, and decide your position in it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product tries to please everyone and reaches no one.
frameworks.guideJa:
誰に売るかを決める型。
市場を分け・狙いを選び・位置を決める。
checks: Segment, target and position follow in order.
The target is chosen from the segments; the position is set for that target.

frameworks.name: SUCCESs
frameworks.summary: Make a message stick: simple, unexpected, concrete, credible, emotional, story.
frameworks.whenToUse: A message is correct but nobody remembers it.
frameworks.guideJa:
伝わるメッセージにする型。
6 つの項目ごとに、言い方を直す。
checks: All six are about the same one message.
Each item has its quality (simple, unexpected, and so on).

frameworks.name: SWOT Analysis
frameworks.summary: Sort strengths and weaknesses inside, and opportunities and threats outside.
frameworks.whenToUse: A strategy needs a quick picture of the position.
frameworks.guideJa:
自分の立ち位置をつかむ型。
内と外、プラスとマイナスで、4 つの所に書く。
checks: S and W are internal and now.
O and T are external and outside control.
Cells hold facts, not plans.

frameworks.name: Systems Thinking (Causal Loop)
frameworks.nameJa: システム思考（因果ループ）
frameworks.origin: Jay W. Forrester; Peter M. Senge
frameworks.summary: See a problem as loops of causes that feed each other over time.
frameworks.whenToUse: Fixes make things worse later, or a problem keeps growing.
frameworks.guideJa:
原因が回り回る仕組みを見る型。
要素をつなぎ、どう強め合うかを書く。
checks: Factors form a loop with arrows.
Each arrow raises (+) or lowers (-) the next.
The loop is reinforcing or balancing.

frameworks.name: TAPS
frameworks.summary: To be, as is, problem, solution: state the gap, then the fix.
frameworks.whenToUse: A proposal must be explained briefly and logically.
frameworks.guideJa:
提案を筋道立てて話す型。
ありたい姿・今・問題・解決策の順に書く。
checks: To be and as is are two states of the same item.
The problem is the gap; the solution closes it.

frameworks.name: Task Inventory Sheet
frameworks.summary: List every task with its owner, time, and frequency.
frameworks.whenToUse: Workload is too high or uneven and nobody knows where the hours go.
frameworks.guideJa:
仕事の量を見える形にする型。
業務ごとに、担当・時間・回数を書く。
checks: Each task has an owner, hours and frequency.
Tasks do not overlap.

frameworks.name: Time Machine Method
frameworks.summary: Imagine you stand in the future where things went well, then look back on the path.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person is stuck in today's limits.
frameworks.guideJa:
未来から今を見る型。
うまくいった未来から、やってきたことをさかのぼって書く。
checks: The path is written backward from the future.
What was done at each point leads to the situation at the next point.

lanes: What I did やったこと

frameworks.name: Tuckman's Stages
frameworks.summary: Teams grow through forming, storming, norming, and performing.
frameworks.whenToUse: A new team has conflict and the person wonders if it is normal.
frameworks.guideJa:
チームが育つ段階を見る型。
今どの段階かと、その様子を書く。
checks: Stages follow in order.
The current stage follows from the observed behavior of the team.

frameworks.name: Two-Factor Theory
frameworks.summary: Some factors only remove dissatisfaction; others create motivation.
frameworks.whenToUse: Pay or conditions improved but motivation did not.
frameworks.guideJa:
やる気の元を分ける型。
不満を消すものと、やる気を生むものを書く。
checks: Hygiene factors cause dissatisfaction when missing; motivators create motivation when present.
The two are not swapped.

frameworks.name: Urgency / Importance Matrix
frameworks.nameJa: 緊急度・重要度マトリクス
frameworks.origin: Dwight D. Eisenhower; Stephen R. Covey
frameworks.summary: Sort tasks by urgency and importance to decide what to do, plan, hand off, or drop.
frameworks.whenToUse: The person is busy all day and the important work never starts.
frameworks.guideJa:
やることの順を決める型。
急ぐかと大事かで、やることを 4 つの所に置く。
checks: Each item is placed by urgency and importance.
Do now is both.

frameworks.name: Value Analysis / Engineering
frameworks.summary: Value is function divided by cost; keep the functions and cut the cost.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product or service costs too much and quality must stay.
frameworks.guideJa:
品質を落とさず費用を下げる型。
機能ごとに、今の費用と案を書く。
checks: Each function has its cost now.
Ideas keep the function and lower the cost (value = function / cost).

frameworks.name: Value Chain
frameworks.summary: Split the business into activities and see which ones add value or cost.
frameworks.whenToUse: Margins are thin and the person asks where value is made or lost.
frameworks.guideJa:
どの活動で価値が生まれるかを見る型。
活動ごとに、強みと費用を書く。
checks: Activities are primary in order, plus support activities.
Each has evidence of the value or cost it adds.

frameworks.name: Value Proposition Canvas
frameworks.nameJa: バリュー・プロポジション・キャンバス
frameworks.summary: Match the jobs, pains, and gains of a customer with your products, pain relievers, and gain creators.
frameworks.whenToUse: A product exists but the fit with real customer needs is unclear.
frameworks.guideJa:
お客の困りごとと自分の商品を合わせる型。
右にお客、左に自分の商品のことを書く。
checks: Each pain reliever answers a customer pain, and each gain creator answers a customer gain.

columns:
Product 製品
Pain relievers 悩み解消
Gain creators 利得創出

Customer 顧客
Jobs 用事
Pains 悩み
Gains 利得

frameworks.name: VRIO
frameworks.summary: Test a resource: is it valuable, rare, hard to imitate, and backed by the organization?
frameworks.whenToUse: The person asks whether a strength can last.
frameworks.guideJa:
強みが長く続くかを見る型。
資源ごとに、4 つの問いに答える。
checks: Each resource is tested in order: value, rarity, imitability, organization.
A no at any step stops the advantage there.

frameworks.name: Want / Commitment Matrix
frameworks.summary: Place a person by how much they want a goal and how much they act on it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person says they want something but does not move.
frameworks.guideJa:
やりたい気持ちと行動を比べる型。
意欲と行動の量で、自分を置く。
checks: One person sits in one quadrant by want and commitment.
The basis is their words and actions.

frameworks.name: Principles of Influence
frameworks.summary: Six principles that make people say yes: reciprocity, commitment, social proof, authority, liking, scarcity.
frameworks.whenToUse: A message or offer needs to persuade, or the person wants to see how they are being persuaded.
frameworks.guideJa:
人が動く理由を知る型。
6 つの原理ごとに、当てはまる場面を書く。
checks: Each item is a concrete scene or move that uses its principle (reciprocity, commitment, and so on).

frameworks.name: Will / Can / Must
frameworks.summary: Find where what you want, what you can, and what is asked of you overlap.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person or an organization chooses its work or role by what it wants, can, and is asked to do ("our team can do this, so we want to do that").
frameworks.guideJa:
進む方向を見つける型。
やりたい・できる・求められるを書き、重なる所を探す。
checks: All three circles are about the same person or the same organization.
Items in an overlap belong to every circle of that overlap.

frameworks.name: Will / Skill Matrix
frameworks.nameJa: ウィル・スキル・マトリクス
frameworks.summary: Place a member by will and skill to choose how to lead them.
frameworks.whenToUse: A manager does not know how to deal with a member.
frameworks.guideJa:
メンバーへの関わり方を決める型。
意欲とスキルで、メンバーを置く。
checks: One member sits in one quadrant by will and skill for the same task.
The way to lead fits the quadrant.

axes.left: スキル 低 Low skill
axes.right: スキル 高 High skill

frameworks.name: YWT
frameworks.nameJa: YWT（やった・わかった・次やる）
frameworks.summary: Look back with three columns: what I did, what I learned, what I do next.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person or team wants a light review that leads to learning.
frameworks.guideJa:
学びにつなげる振り返りの型。
やったこと・わかったこと・次にやることを書く。
checks: W is what was learned from Y; T is the next action that uses W.

frameworks.name: OKR
frameworks.summary: Set an inspiring objective and a few measurable key results for it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A team needs focus and a shared way to see progress.
frameworks.guideJa:
目指す所に集中する型。
わくわくする目標と、測れる主な結果を 3 つ書く。
checks: The Objective is qualitative.
Each KR is a result with a number, not a task.
The KRs together meet the Objective.

frameworks.name: Logic Model
frameworks.summary: Link inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact of a program.
frameworks.whenToUse: A program or project must show how its work leads to change.
frameworks.guideJa:
活動が変化につながる筋道を見る型。
投入・活動・結果・成果・影響を順に書く。
checks: Each step leads to the next.
Outputs count what was done; Outcomes say what changed.

frameworks.name: Lean Canvas
frameworks.summary: A one-page plan for a startup idea that starts from the problem.
frameworks.whenToUse: A new idea needs a fast check of its riskiest parts.
frameworks.guideJa:
新しい事業の案を素早く確かめる型。
9 つの区画を、課題から順に書く。
checks: Problem, customer, unique value and solution connect through the same customer.
The solution answers the problem.

areas.label:
Customer segments
顧客セグメント

frameworks.name: MECE
frameworks.summary: Split a whole into parts that do not overlap and leave nothing out.
frameworks.whenToUse: A list of points overlaps or misses something.
frameworks.guideJa:
漏れなく重なりなく分ける型。
全体を、重ならない部分に分けて書く。
checks: The parts make the whole, do not overlap, and follow one cut.

frameworks.name: Pyramid Principle
frameworks.nameJa: ピラミッド・ストラクチャー
frameworks.summary: Put the main message on top and the supporting points and facts below it.
frameworks.whenToUse: A report or talk must lead to one clear conclusion.
frameworks.guideJa:
結論が伝わる話にする型。
一番上に結論、その下に理由と事実を書く。
checks: The top is a claim, not a topic.
Each reason supports the claim; each fact supports its reason.
Upward reads as a summary, downward as proof.

frameworks.name: Persona
frameworks.summary: Describe one typical user as a real-looking person, with goals and pains.
frameworks.whenToUse: The team designs for an average user who does not exist.
frameworks.guideJa:
使う人を 1 人の人物として描く型。
名前・暮らし・目標・悩み・1 日を書く。
checks: One imagined person.
Goals and pains are based on real users' voices or facts.

frameworks.name: Jobs to Be Done
frameworks.summary: Customers hire a product to get a job done in a situation; find that job.
frameworks.whenToUse: Customer data says who buys but not why.
frameworks.guideJa:
お客が本当に片づけたい用事を見つける型。
場面・用事・今使っている物・望む結果を書く。
checks: The job is what the customer wants done in a situation, not the product.
The better outcome is the job done well.

rows: Hired now 今使っているもの

frameworks.name: Issue-Driven Framework
frameworks.summary: Find the one question worth answering, then chain strategy, tactics, and tasks down to its answer.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person or a team has an open worry (what should I do?) with many facts but no clear question at its center.

frameworks.name: Four Forms of Thinking
frameworks.summary: Think a subject through four forms in order: divide, compare, infer, and transform, each with two core moves and one optional move.
frameworks.whenToUse: A person is stuck on a subject and needs fresh angles to look at it from.
